Both original BFS/Floyd C++ source algorithms inspected for exhaustive bounds; independent program verifies table.

value.rationale: First complete finite exact equality layer for a published open bipartite extremal problem; small n are mathematically motivated thresholds and one 9-vertex diameter-four graph defeats a natural matching-only ansatz. Provides reproducible nontrivial global finite benchmark, not a generic table without purpose.

final_claim: Among all connected bipartite graphs on n=7,8,9 vertices, gpn maxima are respectively 49,74,105, with exactly 2,2,3 isomorphism types at equality. On 9 vertices, the K4,5 minus two disjoint 2-edge stars gives a diameter-4 coextremizer beyond matching deletion; fixed-shore labeled equality counts are 13,88,420.
limitations: Finite orders 7,8,9 only, never a theorem for larger n.
Counts 13,88,420 refer to fixed named shore assignments, not all fully labeled graphs; equality descriptions up to isomorphism.
